newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Capitel launch ends ETB phone monopoly in Bogota.
newsitem.headline: Capitel launch ends ETB phone monopoly in Bogota.

text.p: State-run Empresas de Telecomunicaciones de Santafe de Bogota (ETB) lost its longstanding monopoly on telephone service in the Colombian capital Friday with the formal launch of a powerful conglomerate called Capitel.
The new company was formed last year through a strategic alliance between Colombia's state-run Telecom and Ericsson SpA, NEC Corp, Nortel Northern Telecom Ltd and Siemens AG.
President Ernesto Samper inaugurated this morning the first of 550,000 telephone lines that will be installed in Bogota and the suburb of Soacha this year and next.

Capitel, which has already torn up Bogota's streets to lay fiber optic cable as part of a mega-project with a $513 million price tag, will operate 14 exchanges from 10 buildings across the city, complete with 550 remote concentrators.
It will compete with ETB in providing both domestic and international telephone service.
ETB was slated for privatization last year, but the move was blocked by workers and members of Bogota's city council.
